senses.en: a group of people who share the same language, culture and origins
examples: Viet Nam has 54 **ethnic groups**.
Each **ethnic group** has its own costume and festivals.
The Tay are the largest **ethnic group** in the north.

forms.en: connected with a group that shares a culture and origin
forms.ex: **Ethnic** costumes are worn at the festival.

senses.en: an ethnic group that is small in number compared with the main group in a country
examples: Many **ethnic minorities** live in the mountains.
The school teaches children from three **ethnic minorities**.
**Ethnic minority** languages are taught in some provinces.

ethnic minority.note: Opposite of *majority*. The plural is *minorit**ies*** — change *y* to *ies*.

senses.en: the largest part of a group; more than half
examples: The **majority** of people here are farmers.
The Kinh are the **majority** in Viet Nam.
A **majority** of students voted for the trip.

majority.note: Opposite: **minority**. With *the majority of + plural noun*, the verb is usually plural: *the majority of students **are** …*

senses.en: a way of behaving that a group of people has followed for a long time
examples: It is a **custom** to give lucky money at Tet.
Every village has its own **customs**.
Taking off your shoes indoors is a local **custom**.

senses.en: the place at a border or airport where officials check what you are bringing in
examples: We waited an hour to get through **customs**.
You must declare it at **customs**.

custom.note: A **custom** is what a group does; a *habit* is what one person does. Compare *tradition*, which is usually older and passed down through generations.

senses.en: the clothes worn by people of a particular place, period or group, especially at a special event
examples: The dancers wore traditional **costume**.
Each ethnic group has its own colourful **costume**.
She made a **costume** for the school play.

costume.note: **Costume** is special or traditional clothing, not everyday clothes — for those use *clothes*. Careful with the spelling: cos-**tume**, not *custom*.

senses.en: a house built on tall posts above the ground or above water
examples: Many ethnic groups live in **stilt houses**.
The **stilt house** keeps the family dry in the rainy season.
We climbed a wooden ladder into the **stilt house**.

forms.en: one of the long posts a building stands on

senses.en: one of a series of flat steps cut into a hillside so that crops can be grown on it
examples: The **terraced fields** of Sa Pa are famous.
Rice is grown on **terraced fields** in the mountains.
The **terraced fields** look like giant steps.

forms.en: a flat level area cut into a slope
forms.ex: Each **terrace** holds a few centimetres of water.

senses.en: the traditions, buildings and culture a country has had for many years and still values
examples: Ha Long Bay is a World **Heritage** Site.
Folk songs are part of our cultural **heritage**.
The village is proud of its **heritage**.

heritage.note: Uncountable — never *heritages*. Stress the first syllable: **HER**-i-tage.

senses.en: a set of actions always performed in the same way, especially as part of a ceremony
examples: The **ritual** is performed at the start of the harvest.
Lighting incense is an important **ritual**.
The wedding follows an ancient **ritual**.

senses.en: something you always do in the same way, out of habit
examples: Sunday lunch with my grandparents is a family **ritual**.
Coffee at seven is his morning **ritual**.

senses.en: a traditional song of a particular region, usually passed on by being sung rather than written down
examples: She sang an old **folk song** at the festival.
**Folk songs** tell the story of the village.
My grandmother taught me three **folk songs**.

forms.en: traditional, belonging to ordinary people of a region

senses.en: a tall tropical plant with hard hollow stems, used for building and making things
examples: Baskets are woven from **bamboo**.
The stilt house is built of **bamboo** and wood.
**Bamboo** grows very quickly.

senses.en: to make cloth or baskets by passing threads or strips over and under each other
examples: The women **weave** cloth on wooden looms.
She learned to **weave** baskets from her mother.
This scarf was **woven** by hand.

forms.ex: She is the best **weaver** in the village.

senses.en: a container made of thin strips of wood, bamboo or cane woven together
examples: She carried the fruit in a bamboo **basket**.
The **baskets** are woven by hand.
Put the eggs in that **basket**.

senses.en: a round metal disc that makes a deep ringing sound when you hit it
examples: The **gong** is played at village ceremonies.
**Gong** culture in the Central Highlands is a World Heritage tradition.
He struck the **gong** three times.

senses.en: a large natural hole in the side of a hill or under the ground
examples: Son Doong is the largest **cave** in the world.
Early people lived in **caves**.
We explored a **cave** near the village.

senses.en: being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else
senses.vi: độc đáo, độc nhất vô nhị
examples: Each ethnic group has its own **unique** costume.
The festival is **unique** to this province.
Every fingerprint is **unique**.

unique.note: Because it means *the only one*, careful writers avoid *very unique* or *quite unique* — something is either unique or it isn't. Pronounced /juˈniːk/: yoo-**NEEK**.

senses.en: very different from each other; of many different kinds
examples: Viet Nam is culturally very **diverse**.
The country has a **diverse** range of landscapes.
Our class is **diverse** — six languages are spoken.

forms.en: the fact of including many different kinds

senses.en: following ideas, customs or methods that have existed for a long time
examples: They wore **traditional** costumes for the festival.
Weaving is a **traditional** craft in this village.
**Traditional** music is played on the gong.

forms.en: a belief or custom passed from one generation to the next
forms.ex: It is a **tradition** to visit relatives at Tet.

forms.en: in the way that has been usual for a long time
